spider-speech.name: Spider-Speech
spider-speech.always: You understand spiders, and they understand you. They live in every corner of the castle, and they notice everything.
spider-speech.daily: Ask the spiders in a room what they saw there since yesterday. The DM answers in a few short, whispery words.
spider-speech.drawback: Spiders want paying: give up a food item from your Bag, or they ignore you until tomorrow. And they will not go anywhere near the covered painting.

fashionably-late.name: Fashionably Late
fashionably-late.always: You are late for everything. But the castle seems to bend around it: you always turn up at exactly the moment things get interesting.
fashionably-late.daily: Burst into a scene or a fight that has already started, wherever the others are. In a fight you join at the start of the next round, and your first spell gets +2 to hit.
fashionably-late.drawback: At every morning class the DM rolls a d20 for you. On 1 to 6 you are late: lose 5 house points, and the teacher remembers your name for the wrong reasons.

green-thumb.name: Green Thumb
green-thumb.always: Plants like you. You know any plant on sight (what it does, and whether it bites), you roll with advantage in Herbology, and you can learn Herbology spells nobody else is taught.
green-thumb.daily: Ask a plant for help: a vine lowers itself for you to climb, a hedge parts, a Mandrake stays quiet, or the grass tells you who walked past.
green-thumb.drawback: Plants feel what you feel. When you are angry or frightened, the plants around you go wild. And Devil’s Snare always grabs you first.

rat-speech.name: Rat-Speech
rat-speech.always: You can talk to rats. They know every crack, pipe and pantry in the castle.
rat-speech.daily: Send a rat to listen in a room or follow someone for one block. At the start of the next block, the DM tells you what it heard.
rat-speech.drawback: Rats are cowards and gossips: on a d20 of 1 to 5, it also tells someone else what you asked. And the caretaker’s cat can smell rat on you, so after curfew you roll with disadvantage to stay hidden.

mirror-self.name: Mirror Self
mirror-self.always: You can make a magical illusion of yourself. It looks, moves and smiles like you, but it cannot speak or touch anything.
mirror-self.daily: For one scene, send your illusion somewhere you are not: as a decoy, an alibi, or to walk into danger first. In a fight, the first attack that would hit you hits the illusion instead, and it pops.
mirror-self.drawback: While it is up you cannot cast spells. If it is hit or touched it bursts, and you feel it: 1d4 damage. And something else in this castle copies people. It has noticed you.

battered-suitcase.name: The Battered Suitcase
battered-suitcase.always: You carry an old suitcase with the initials N.S. worn into the handle. Inside is a whole world of magical creatures, and they let you in.
battered-suitcase.daily: Let one creature out to help for a scene: a Niffler sniffs out something shiny or hidden, a Bowtruckle picks a small lock, or an Occamy squeezes into any gap to fetch something.
battered-suitcase.drawback: Things get out. Each morning the DM rolls a d20: on 1 to 4, something escaped in the night and is causing chaos somewhere in the castle. Catch it before a teacher does, or the case is confiscated. Professor Scamander would very much like to know where you got it.

invisibility-cloak.name: The Invisibility Cloak
invisibility-cloak.always: You own a real Invisibility Cloak, silvery and light as water. Under it, nobody can see you.
invisibility-cloak.daily: Its old magic tires: wear it for one scene a day. Unseen, you can slip past anyone, and in a fight your first attack has advantage (after that, they know where you are).
invisibility-cloak.drawback: It hides you, not your sound, your smell or your footprints: the Marauder’s Map still shows you, creatures smell you, ghosts walk straight through you, and Quill’s Sight sees a shimmer. Two can hide under it only if both pass a DEX roll. If a teacher catches you in it, it is confiscated for a week.

blackwood.name: Blackwood
blackwood.secret: Your grandmother’s diary mentions “the painted man” and a debt the Blackwoods never paid. Centuries ago, a Blackwood sealed a dark wizard inside a painting.

sinclair.name: Sinclair
sinclair.secret: Your sister wrote home that the castle “feels wrong this year” and asked you to keep an eye out. You’re the only one she told.

fenwick.name: Fenwick
fenwick.secret: Your great-uncle copied the Marauder’s Map before he was expelled, but it was torn in half during a duel. Someone at Hogwarts has the other half, and they’ve been watching you.

thornbury.name: Thornbury
thornbury.secret: Last year your family’s prize hippogriff, Bramble, vanished near the Forbidden Forest. Nobody believed you when you said you heard her calling.

quill.name: Quill
quill.secret: On the train, you’ll be the only one who sees the covered painting’s eyes follow you. It happens again every time you pass one of its kind.

marlowe.name: Marlowe
marlowe.secret: Your vault holds only a few coins and an old iron key with a serpent on it. An ancestor served a dark wizard, and only a Parseltongue can open the door that key belongs to.

hale.name: Hale
hale.secret: Your great-grandmother kept a casebook. One page describes a Hogwarts student brought in long ago, alive but empty, “as if someone had painted over her”. She kept whispering one word: Vale. The case was closed by order of the Headmaster.

penrose.name: Penrose
penrose.secret: Your great-great-grandmother once sat for a famous portrait painter. She came home unable to change her face ever again. The painting was never delivered, and nobody knows where it went.

okafor.name: Okafor
okafor.secret: Last month Gringotts sent your mum to inspect a painting before it was shipped to Hogwarts. She refused to unwrap it and wrote one word in her report: Occupied. It was sent anyway.

rune-tablet-1.name: Rune tablet (beasts and sky)
rune-tablet-1.note: Pictures, each with a word in runes underneath

read.heading: A cracked slate from the Ancient Runes shelf
read.footer: Each rune is always the same letter. Pencil what you work out into your rune notebook.

rune-tablet-2.name: Rune tablet (garden)
rune-tablet-2.note: Pictures, each with a word in runes underneath

read.heading: A mossy slate wedged under a seed tray
read.footer: Each rune is always the same letter. Pencil what you work out into your rune notebook.

rune-tablet-3.name: Rune tablet (hearth)
rune-tablet-3.note: Pictures, each with a word in runes underneath

read.heading: A soot-black slate from beside a fireplace
read.footer: Each rune is always the same letter. Pencil what you work out into your rune notebook.

diary-page.name: Page of Vale’s diary
diary-page.note: Written in runes. Collect all three.

read.heading: Pages of a diary, in a spiky hand
pages: ONLY THE ONE WHO STANDS ALONE
read.footer: Each rune is always the same letter. With all three pages, show the DM: the whole diary goes up on the TV.

map-half.name: Half of the Marauder’s Map
map-half.note: Torn down the middle. It wakes only for the right words

read.heading: Scratched along the torn edge
pages: I SOLEMNLY SWEAR THAT I AM UP TO NO GOOD
read.footer: Tiny runes in faded ink. Ask the DM to put them on the TV so you can work them out together.

ring-clue-serpent.name: Scratched note (first ring)
ring-clue-serpent.note: “The first ring remembers what sleeps beneath the castle.”

read.text: “The first ring remembers what sleeps beneath the castle.”

ring-clue-moon.name: Star chart (second ring)
ring-clue-moon.note: “The second ring follows the lamp of the night.”

read.text: “The second ring follows the lamp of the night.”

ring-clue-owl.name: Feathered card (last ring)
ring-clue-owl.note: “The last ring belongs to the one who carries every letter.”

read.text: “The last ring belongs to the one who carries every letter.”

sword-of-gryffindor.name: The Sword of Gryffindor
sword-of-gryffindor.lore: A silver blade set with rubies. It can’t be owned, only earned: it comes to a true Gryffindor in their darkest moment, pulled from the old Sorting Hat.
sword-of-gryffindor.always: While you hold it you can’t be frightened, and your spells deal +2 damage to anything Vale has made.
sword-of-gryffindor.daily: Strike with the blade itself: d20 + STR to hit, 3d8 damage. Anything painted, Vale included, takes double.
sword-of-gryffindor.drawback: It stays for one fight only. When the danger has passed, it is simply gone, until it is needed again.
sword-of-gryffindor.found: Day 7 in the Undercroft, when a student does something truly brave: they pull it from the Sorting Hat.

phoenix-tear.name: A Phoenix Tear
phoenix-tear.lore: A single tear in a crystal vial, given freely by a phoenix to someone who stayed loyal when it would have been easier to run.
phoenix-tear.always: The vial is warm to the touch. Paint Wraiths and other dark things hesitate: they attack you with disadvantage.
phoenix-tear.daily: Once ever: one drop heals anyone to full HP and lifts every curse and status on them, or wakes one drained student completely.
phoenix-tear.drawback: There is only one drop. Once it is used, it is gone for ever.
phoenix-tear.found: The Hospital Wing, after a student risks themselves to protect someone else.

vales-first-brush.name: Vale’s First Brush
vales-first-brush.lore: The brush Corvin Vale painted his first living portrait with. Three hundred years on, the bristles are still wet.
vales-first-brush.always: You feel paint the way others feel weather: you always know when something painted is close.
vales-first-brush.daily: Paint a doorway on any wall and it is a real door for one scene. Or paint over a wound: heal 2d6.
vales-first-brush.drawback: Every use adds 1 Corruption, and Vale feels it. He starts talking to you. He is very persuasive.
vales-first-brush.found: The Undercroft, or offered by the covered painting as part of The Painter’s Bargain.

blackwood-seal.name: The Blackwood Seal Ring
blackwood-seal.lore: The ring a Blackwood pressed into hot wax three hundred years ago, to seal Corvin Vale inside his own canvas.
blackwood-seal.always: Painted magic can’t take hold of you: the Painted Double can’t copy you, and Vale can’t drain you.
blackwood-seal.daily: Press the ring to a door, a frame or a painting: it is sealed shut for the rest of the day. Nothing comes out, nothing goes in.
blackwood-seal.drawback: Vale knows this ring. Paint Wraiths always go for you first, and from Day 5 the painting whispers to you at night.
blackwood-seal.found: Given by a Blackwood portrait (best of all to the Blackwood), or hidden behind the oldest shield in the Trophy Room.

dark-room-lantern.name: The Lantern of the Dark Room
dark-room-lantern.lore: A small iron lantern waiting at the way out of the mirror maze. Its flame is cold and blue, and it has never gone out.
dark-room-lantern.always: You are never in the dark: no spell, wind or water can put your light out.
dark-room-lantern.daily: Hold it up to a wall, a page or a painting: invisible writing, hidden doors and secret marks show in its light.
dark-room-lantern.drawback: In its light, anything painted can see you too. While it is lit, you can’t hide from Vale’s servants.
dark-room-lantern.found: The way out of the Mirror in the Dark.

moonlit-compass.name: The Moonlit Compass
moonlit-compass.lore: A brass compass with no north, south, east or west. Its needle is a sliver of moonlight.
moonlit-compass.always: You can never truly be lost: you always know the way back to your common room.
moonlit-compass.daily: Ask it what you need most. The needle points: the DM tells you which way, and roughly how far.
moonlit-compass.drawback: It points to what you need, not what you want. Sometimes that is a person you would rather avoid.
moonlit-compass.found: The Astronomy Tower at night, or the ancient chest in the Room of Requirement.

old-boot.name: The Old Boot
old-boot.lore: A mouldy, laceless boot. It is secretly a Portkey, charmed long ago and never collected.
old-boot.daily: Once: everyone touching it is whisked to one place the holder names, anywhere in the castle or the grounds. Count to three and grab on.
old-boot.drawback: The landing is rough: everyone takes 1d4 and is dizzy for a round. Afterwards, it is just a boot.
old-boot.found: Under the floorboards of the Shrieking Shack.

twin-cabinet-key.name: The Twin Cabinet Key
twin-cabinet-key.lore: A tarnished key that fits any wardrobe or cupboard in the castle, and opens it onto its twin, deep in the Room of Requirement.
twin-cabinet-key.daily: Step into any cupboard or wardrobe and come out in the Room of Requirement, or the other way round. Up to three can go together.
twin-cabinet-key.drawback: Something else knows the way too. Each time, the DM rolls a d20: on a 1, something has followed you through.

goblin-dagger.name: The Goblin-Silver Dagger
goblin-dagger.lore: Goblin-made silver, older than Hogwarts. It takes in only what makes it stronger.
goblin-dagger.always: It never dulls and never tarnishes, and it cuts through any rope, vine or magical binding (Devil’s Snare included).
goblin-dagger.daily: Strike with it for 2d6. Against painted things it drinks the paint: after it hits one, its next hit deals +1d6.
goblin-dagger.drawback: Goblins believe what they make still belongs to them. A polite, unmistakable letter from Gringotts will ask for it back.
goblin-dagger.found: The cursed chest in the Shrieking Shack, or by owl from Okafor’s mum: “Keep this safe, and don’t tell the goblins.”

silver-memory.name: The Silver Memory
silver-memory.lore: A stoppered vial of silver mist: someone’s memory, saved three hundred years ago.
silver-memory.daily: Once: pour it out and the whole table sees the memory. The DM tells the scene: a night in the castle when Corvin Vale still walked its halls.
silver-memory.drawback: Memories pull. Whoever pours it is lost in it for the rest of the scene, and wakes cold and shaking (−3 HP).
silver-memory.found: The Restricted Section, or a gift from the Headmaster after the second drained student.

lock.title: The Turning Lock
lock.intro: Three stone rings, each carved with symbols. Turn them until the right three symbols sit beneath the arrow.
lock.solution: Serpent, Moon, Owl. Clues: “what sleeps beneath the castle” (the serpent in the Undercroft), “the lamp of the night” (the moon), “the one who carries every letter” (an owl).

bottles.title: The Seven Bottles
bottles.intro: Seven bottles stand in a row. One lets you walk on through the fire. One leads safely back. Two bring a deep sleep. Three are poison. Only one of you may drink to go forward.
clues: No poison stands beside the way back.
No two poisons stand side by side.
The way back stands beside a sleeping draught.
The way forward is neither red nor clear.
The way forward stands somewhere to the left of the way back.
bottles.solution: Bottle 4, the small gold one. Poison: 1, 3, 5. Sleep: 2, 6. Back: 7. (Checked: these six clues allow only this answer, and every clue is needed.)
